D009_m001.question:
Lately… well, actually for about the past year, I’ve just felt empty. Like nothing matters—not my work, not hanging out with the guys, not even coming home to my wife. I used to love working on cars in the garage on weekends, but now the tools just sit there. I’m tired all the time, even after sleeping. My body feels like it’s made of concrete. Some days, when I’m on the lift working high up on a job, this sudden urge hits me—just to let go, to step off. I don’t plan it, wouldn’t do it, but the thought flashes, and it scares me.

But before this, about a year ago, it was the opposite. I was wired. Didn’t need sleep—could work 16 hours, come home, start renovating the basement, talk for hours to anyone who’d listen. My wife said I wouldn’t shut up, like words were spilling out. I had this buzz inside I couldn’t slow down. Felt unstoppable. I was also… randy as hell—texting exes, flirting with anyone. It was like I didn’t care. That lasted a month, maybe. Boss said I was getting things done, so no problems at work. But now? I can barely get out of bed.

    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

The things that used to matter—my job, my wife, even the train routes I’ve memorized for years—feel empty. I can’t get myself to do much of anything. I wake up tired, even after eight hours. I started keeping a mental tally of every little thing, convinced I deserve to pay for it. A few weeks ago, I filled a plastic bag with pills. I didn’t go through with it, but… I had it ready, just in case the weight got too bad.  

Before that, though—last winter—I was the opposite. I barely slept, but I didn’t care. Felt wired, like I could work two shifts back-to-back. I didn’t feel sick then—just… alive. Too alive.  

But driving trains, you can’t shake. You’ve got to be steady. And right now? I don’t feel steady at all.
